key_insight: In uncertainty-aware distribution grids, local electricity markets can cut customer and system costs while revealing that battery value depends strongly on where, when, and alongside what other DERs the batteries are deployed.
engineering_relevance: For grid planners, the results suggest that market design, PV expansion, and storage siting should be co-optimized because poorly placed batteries can worsen congestion while well-sited ones improve both reliability and economics.
method: Modeled PV generation uncertainty with an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process to preserve temporal correlation.
Ran rolling-horizon alternating optimal power flow on the IEEE 123-node feeder.
Compared flat tariff, real-time pricing, and local electricity market designs across storage and solar penetration levels.
evidence_signal: Evaluation on the IEEE 123-node feeder shows the local electricity market achieves the lowest customer and system costs under uncertainty, outperforming other markets across most storage and solar penetration cases.
watch_item: Local electricity markets may worsen customer outcomes at very low PV penetration, so deployment should be paired with sufficient PV growth before scaling storage.
paper_title: Understanding the role and value of battery storage in renewables-rich distribution grids under uncertainty and different market paradigms
